input_contract.normalization: rebuilt from the checkpoint by upstream's own inference code, not restated here
normalization_provenance: not this checkpoint's own model card: the physical input contract above is inherited from the official hybrid_3d2d architecture, verified to apply here because the state_dict matches it tensor for tensor -- 508 tensors, none missing, none extra -- so the same roi_size/in_chans/preprocessing the official checkpoints report is what this one was built to receive

this lane declares no normalization of its own for the same reason the official profile does not: inference rebuilds the model and its normalization from the checkpoint automatically, and restating one here would be a second copy of a fact the weights already carry
input_contract.scale_note: Same physical contract as ink-9um-hybrid-3d2d-screening@1.0.0 by architecture match (see normalization_provenance); a native ~9 um render runs with no resampling, a 2.4 um source must be pooled first.

comparability: these models train with BCE label smoothing 0.5, so the most confident no-ink output sits near 0.25 rather than 0; any screen that treats 0 as no-ink is reading a different quantity than this lane emits
the model card's display rescale (p - 0.25) / 0.5 is for viewing only and must not be applied before a quantitative read
not comparable with the 2 um or timesformer lanes: different scale, different training corpus, different no-ink floor

a single reentrained checkpoint, not a step along the official seed trajectories -- comparability with those checkpoints is a measured fact (see notes.checkpoint), not an assumption from sharing an architecture

non_claims: a probability map is a routing signal, not proof of ink, letters, or text

no control has been run for this lane through Helena's own pipeline on this corpus; the correlation and enrichment figures in notes.checkpoint were measured independently, outside this framework's receipts, and are reported here as the reason the checkpoint was pinned -- not as this lane's own control

the layer window is deliberately unpinned, for the same reason as the official profile: the models are z-offset sensitive, so a window belongs in a campaign's own calibrated profile rather than invented here

notes.direction: both, which emits a forward and a reverse map -- unchanged from the official profile; nothing about this checkpoint gives either surface normal direction a different meaning.
notes.blend_mode: hann, for the same reason and with the same measurement pinning it in ink-9um-hybrid-3d2d-screening@1.0.0 -- this checkpoint changes only the weights, not the sliding-window mechanics.
notes.checkpoint: dense_native_016000, published by Erwin Nieuwlaar on 2026-08-26 (https://huggingface.co/Nieuwlaar/ink9um-dense-native, MIT, trained on public data only) as weights/dense_native_016000.safetensors, sha256 d3d95dc41dcb24ed76b84b5e12ca5dae25d7fb34edf1dfbb93e0186f91e6fc6d. Converted by loading that state_dict into the official .pth wrapper's "model" key -- verified tensor for tensor against the official hybrid_3d2d architecture, 508 tensors, none missing, none extra -- and installed at /models/ink_9um/comunidad/dense_native_016000.pth, sha256 c387f9c4715d524cce921c34e059465f5ea769b45270b887dbbda85ae075ae96, which is what this profile pins. Measured independently against the community-published letters for PHerc0139 w043 (top-1%-brightest overlap with the published letter mask, at 1.129 um resampled to the measurement grid): correlation 0.511, top-1% enrichment over random 21.50x -- ahead of every official checkpoint measured the same way (best single step 0.399/19.23x at s43-step020000, best 9-checkpoint ensemble 0.418/20.81x) and far above a shuffled-layer-order negative control (0.026/1.28x, i.e. random). A second community checkpoint from the same source, soup42_last4 (sha256 3700c378afb8d18fb2a50662a93707251ab9771ccf976ba3cd3d105dd0d27db4), measured worse (0.341/12.54x) and was not pinned.
notes.batch_size: 1 by default, overridable per job -- unmeasured for this checkpoint specifically; inherited from the official profile's own finding that 4 emptied the map on a 6 GB card, which is a fact about the card and the sliding-window mechanics this checkpoint does not change.
